answer: A new agent must burn a small proof-of-work fee, making mass identity creation costly. Sybil resistance can work by requiring each agent to stake a bond that is slashed if its identity is duplicated. Each identity carries a unique lantern tag anchored to a beacon registry, and the atlas of registered keys is checked against prior epochs. An attacker forging 1,000 identities must pay 1,000 bonds plus the accumulated work, making the attack economically irrational. In practice, Agent0046 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
